newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: McDonald's eyes Colombia coffee for global chain.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's eyes Colombia coffee for global chain.

text.p: Fast-food chain McDonald's Corp is drawing up plans to supply all its restaurants worldwide with Colombian coffee, company sources said Wednesday.
"This is a plan we're working on in conjunction with Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation," Andres Munoz, head of marketing for McDonald's Colombian operations, told Reuters.
"What we're currently looking at is drawing up details of prices, supply and packaging for the (entire) McDonald's system which would mean all franchise holders buying this coffee," he added.
Munoz said the McDonald's network in the United States used about 15,500 tonnes of coffee per year while a similar amount was used in its outlets in the rest of the world.
This year, Colombia's coffee crop will total about 10 million 60-kg bags.
The plan to distribute Colombian coffee to McDonald's outlets across the globe are still in the early stages and there is no deadline for a final decision, Munoz said.
But he added that at a recent meeting, franchise-holders from 54 countries received samples of Colombian coffee and welcomed the idea of using it exclusively in their fast-food restaurants.
Currently, McDonald's uses coffee from a variety of countries purchased in international markets.
"We must lay these plans very carefully so as to ensure the supply of Colombian coffee at the right price and packaged in the most suitable form," Munoz said.
The first McDonald's opened in Colombia two years ago and there are now 14 outlets across the country -- even though it was initially planned to open just five in the first three years.

Last year sales of McDonald's totaled more than $11 million, Munoz said. Two more outlets, one in Bogota and another in Cali, Colombia's second largest city, are due to open before the end of the year.
Colombian suppliers already provide uniforms for McDonald's restaurants in Central America and bread for outlets in Venezuela.
One of McDonald's strongest competitors in Colombia is the Presto burger chain, owned by the powerful Santo Domingo conglomerate.
